clue.text: Second husband captured by wicked group

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
wicked and cool are both slang for excellent
h is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A woman's second husband is taken by a gang of villains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like evil but is used in its slang sense of excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a group, especially of fish or of people sharing a doctrine or style.

clue.text: Biscuit containers overturned

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: pans are cooking containers

explanation.surface: Biscuit tins have been knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap, as in ginger snap, is a crisp thin biscuit.

clue.text: See 11
Music with strong beat — piano work

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: A description of a rhythmic piano composition, as if reviewing a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular chart music is typically built on a strong, steady rhythm, so the short form of popular fits.

clue.text: Parasites in Hull controlled

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another places it inside

blocks.note: a hull is the outer casing of a seed, a pod
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: An infestation in the English port of Hull is brought under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' poses as the Yorkshire city, but it is the seed casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Policed means kept in order or regulated, a synonym for controlled in the past tense.

clue.text: Gym enthusiast without a pulse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the pieces wrap around a letter

blocks.note: PE is physical education, gym class at school
a nut is a fanatic, as in health nut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic is found to have no heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' seems to be a heartbeat, but here it is the edible seed of a legume.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the seed of a leguminous plant, and the peanut is a legume.

clue.text: Seething realtors go for expert on houses?

indicators.note: seething suggests boiling turmoil, so the letters are churned up

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Angry estate agents call in a property expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The houses are the twelve divisions of the zodiac chart, not homes; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer interprets the twelve houses of a horoscope, so is a specialist in a different kind of house.

clue.text: Hurt in match — leaves boxing?

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match
to ache is to hurt

explanation.surface: A boxer injured during a bout leaves the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves boxing' reads as quitting the sport; it means a container boxing up tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a wooden crate for shipping tea leaves, so it is something that boxes leaves.

clue.text: Cast iron case for storyline?

indicators.note: metal that is cast is poured and moulded into a new form, so the letters are remoulded

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A foundry worker wonders whether a cast-iron box could carry a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast iron' reads as one familiar phrase, but 'Cast' is split off to work on 'iron case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a film or play, a synonym for storyline.

clue.text: European flower festival

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for European
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A spring flower show held somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian spring feast celebrating the resurrection, a religious festival.

clue.text: Limit in accepting love and kindness

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: compass can mean the bounds or limits of an area or scope
taken as written
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to set boundaries while still offering affection and warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is sympathetic concern for others' suffering, a close synonym for kindness.

clue.text: Altered recipe is risk — but it has 2, 20 & 4 Across!

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook warns that changing a recipe is risky, but the dish still has its signature features.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point to SNAP, CRACKLE and POP, the three elf mascots of Kellogg's puffed-rice breakfast cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap, Crackle and Pop are the cartoon characters on the cereal's packaging, named for the sound it makes with milk.

clue.text: Base? Those last seen in Nevada will think Area 51!

indicators.note: the final characters of each word that follows are the only ones taken

blocks.note: the last letter of each of these three words
A is the abbreviation for area
51 in Roman numerals is L (50) plus I (1)

explanation.surface: Anyone who last saw something mysterious over Nevada will think of Area 51, the secret base of UFO lore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a nod to the military base at Area 51, but it is the chemical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an alkali is a soluble base, a substance that neutralises acids.

clue.text: Female domestic needing no male help

indicators.note: to need no item is to do without it, so it is dropped

blocks.note: a maid is a female household servant
m is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A housekeeper who can manage without a man's help.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is assistance, a synonym for help as either noun or verb.

clue.text: Worker is on old spies list at first withdrawn

indicators.note: only the opening character of the word before it is wanted

blocks.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple
taken as written
o is the abbreviation for old
the CIA is the US intelligence agency
the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: An employee appears on an old list of spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Antisocial can mean unsociable, avoiding company, which is what being withdrawn describes.

clue.text: Given praise, lover no longer rang

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a bell that tolled rang slowly

explanation.surface: A spurned partner rings up, full of compliments now the affair is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so extolled means given praise, both past participles.

clue.text: One to examine canine depression first?

blocks.note: a dent is a small hollow pressed into a surface
1st, with the numeral 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A vet asks whether a gloomy dog should be checked before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' suggests a dog and 'depression' a low mood, but the canine is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist inspects teeth, and a canine is one of the pointed teeth beside the incisors.

clue.text: Potentially harm an ET? He's from this planet!

indicators.note: potentially means in a possible form, so the letters may be rearranged into another

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried question whether someone from Earth might hurt a visiting alien.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthman, in science fiction, is a native of Earth as opposed to an alien.

clue.text: Jockey taking very good gee-gee over the top?

blocks.note: pi is informal for pious, i.e. very good or sanctimonious
gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, pronounced as the letters G G
OTT is the common abbreviation for over the top

explanation.surface: A rider on a fine horse goes too far, perhaps over a jump.
explanation.walkthrough: Lester Piggott was a famous British flat-racing jockey, winner of nine Derbys.
explanation.definitionFit: Lester Piggott is an example of a jockey, one of the best-known in British racing history.

clue.text: This writer's books around store due soon

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the earlier pieces wrap the following one

blocks.note: the writer referring to themself: I am, shortened to I'm
NT is the New Testament, the books of the Bible's second part
a mine is a store or rich supply

explanation.surface: An author's books will soon be on sale in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminent means about to happen, so something due soon.

clue.text: Sunbathing's end in Punta Negra?

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's sunbathing comes to an end at a beach resort called Punta Negra.
explanation.definitionFit: A tan is the end result or aim of sunbathing; end here means goal or outcome.

clue.text: Laugh raucously about Republican making noise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: to cackle is to laugh loudly and harshly
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone cackles loudly at a Republican politician, creating a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is a series of sharp snapping sounds, a kind of noise.

clue.text: Ford saloon's horizontal post?

blocks.note: to ford a river is to cross it
a saloon is a bar for drinking

explanation.surface: It sounds like a part of a Ford saloon car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford saloon' suggests the car maker and a car body style; both words are used in other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbar is a horizontal bar, as on a goal frame where it joins the upright posts.

clue.text: Flattery from British State?

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
to state something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the British government deals in flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation; it is the verb meaning say.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter, as in buttering someone up, means flattery used to win favour.

clue.text: Minute liver perhaps seen in journalist?

blocks.note: m is the abbreviation for minute
the liver is an example of a bodily organ

explanation.surface: A tiny liver, as if found in a reporter during surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Morgan is a well-known British journalist and broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Piers Morgan is an example of a journalist, a former tabloid editor turned TV presenter.

clue.text: Excellent returns after accounts shown in plant

indicators.note: something that returns goes back, so in this down entry the word is read upwards

blocks.note: AC is short for account; written twice as a plural
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: Excellent profits after the accounts are published by a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory, but it is a botanical plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub with yellow or white flowers, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Stylish welcome received in clubs twice

indicators.note: something received is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games, written twice
hi is a word of greeting

explanation.surface: A fashionable person is greeted warmly at two nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means elegantly fashionable, a synonym for stylish.

clue.text: Her contact mistaken for Whitehall scientist

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so these letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's contact in government is misidentified as a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the London street of government ministries, so it stands for the British civil service.
explanation.definitionFit: A technocrat is a technical expert wielding power in government, so a scientist in the corridors of power.

clue.text: Champ, caught, fell

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
to fell a tree is to hew it down

explanation.surface: A champion boxer is caught and goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion, but it is the verb meaning to munch noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or bite noisily, as a horse champs its bit, so it means chew.

clue.text: Attack wise man defending Authorised Version

indicators.note: a defender surrounds and protects, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a sage is a wise person
AV is the usual abbreviation for the Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A sage is attacked for defending the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To savage is to attack fiercely, physically or with harsh criticism; both are verbs.

clue.text: Garments hang on one end of line

indicators.note: only the final character of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: to linger is to hang about or around
I is the Roman numeral for one
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Instructions for hanging clothes at the end of a washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear and nightwear, a class of garments.

clue.text: Old English port or whisky?

blocks.note: first meaning: a historic town in East Sussex, one of the Cinque Ports
second meaning: a whiskey distilled mainly from this grain

explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports were a medieval group of harbour towns on England's south-east coast; this one is now inland.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a Sussex town, once a port, and the grain behind a style of whiskey.
